\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{নিয়তি} (niyôti)}{নিয়তি (niyôti)}]{\bn{নিয়তি} (niyôti) — destiny; fate}

\label{lesson:BN-C532-niyoti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an outline, then the Bengali for to leave out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{নিয়তি}}
\textbf{\bn{নিয়তি}} — \emph{niyôti} — \textquotedblleft{}destiny; fate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দাদু} \bn{বলেন}, \bn{নিয়তি} \bn{কেউ} \bn{বদলাতে} \bn{পারে} \bn{না।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dādu bôlen, niyôti keu bôdlāte pāre nā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather says no one can change destiny.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{নিয়তি}} (\emph{niyôti}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{niyati}, \textquotedblleft{}the fixed order of things, destiny\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{niyôti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{niyôti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Dādu bôlen, niyôti keu bôdlāte pāre nā.} — My grandfather says no one can change destiny.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an outline, then the Bengali for to leave out, then say \emph{niyôti} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{নিয়তি} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Destiny; fate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ভবিতব্য} (bhôbitôbyô)}{ভবিতব্য (bhôbitôbyô)}]{\bn{ভবিতব্য} (bhôbitôbyô) — what is bound to happen}

\label{lesson:BN-C532-bhobitobyo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to leave out, then the Bengali for destiny.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ভবিতব্য}}
\textbf{\bn{ভবিতব্য}} — \emph{bhôbitôbyô} — \textquotedblleft{}what is bound to happen\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ট্রেনটা} \bn{ছেড়ে} \bn{গেল}; \bn{এটাই} \bn{ভবিতব্য} \bn{ছিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ṭrenṭā chheṛe gelô; eṭāi bhôbitôbyô chhilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The train left; it was bound to happen.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ভবিতব্য}} (\emph{bhôbitôbyô}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{bhavitavya}, \textquotedblleft{}what is to be\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), from \emph{bhū}, \textquotedblleft{}to be\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhôbitôbyô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhôbitôbyô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Ṭrenṭā chheṛe gelô; eṭāi bhôbitôbyô chhilô.} — The train left; it was bound to happen.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to leave out, then the Bengali for destiny, then say \emph{bhôbitôbyô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{আঁচ} \bn{করা} (ā̃ch kôrā)}{আঁচ করা (ā̃ch kôrā)}]{\bn{আঁচ} \bn{করা} (ā̃ch kôrā) — to sense; to guess (what is coming)}

\label{lesson:BN-C532-ach-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for destiny, then the Bengali for what is bound to happen.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{আঁচ} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{আঁচ} \bn{করা}} — \emph{ā̃ch kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to sense; to guess (what is coming)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আকাশ} \bn{দেখে} \bn{আমি} \bn{ঝড়ের} \bn{আঁচ} \bn{করলাম।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ākāsh dekhe āmi jhôṛer ā̃ch kôrlām.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Looking at the sky, I sensed a storm coming.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{বিপদটা} \bn{আঁচ} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini bipôdṭā ā̃ch kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{আঁচ} \bn{করা}} (\emph{ā̃ch kôrā}) joins \bn{আঁচ}, \textquotedblleft{}an inkling, a rough guess\textquotedblright{}, to \bn{করা}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Bengali \emph{ā̃cā}, \textquotedblleft{}to estimate\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{añcati}, \textquotedblleft{}bends\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 166).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā̃ch kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Ākāsh dekhe āmi jhôṛer ā̃ch kôrlām.} — Looking at the sky, I sensed a storm coming.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for destiny, then the Bengali for what is bound to happen, then say \emph{ā̃ch kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পূর্বাভাস} (pūrbābhās)}{পূর্বাভাস (pūrbābhās)}]{\bn{পূর্বাভাস} (pūrbābhās) — a forecast}

\label{lesson:BN-C532-purbabhas}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for what is bound to happen, then the Bengali for to sense trouble coming.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পূর্বাভাস}}
\textbf{\bn{পূর্বাভাস}} — \emph{pūrbābhās} — \textquotedblleft{}a forecast\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{পূর্বাভাস} \bn{ভালো} \bn{হলে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{কাল} \bn{নৌকায়} \bn{নদী} \bn{পার} \bn{হব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pūrbābhās bhālo hôle āmrā kāl noukāy nôdī pār hôbô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the forecast is good, we'll cross the river by boat tomorrow.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পূর্বাভাস}} (\emph{pūrbābhās}) joins Sanskrit \emph{pūrva}, \textquotedblleft{}before, earlier\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{ābhāsa}, \textquotedblleft{}light, appearance\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams): a first glimpse of what is coming.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pūrbābhās}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pūrbābhās}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Pūrbābhās bhālo hôle āmrā kāl noukāy nôdī pār hôbô.} — If the forecast is good, we'll cross the river by boat tomorrow.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for what is bound to happen, then the Bengali for to sense trouble coming, then say \emph{pūrbābhās} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{পূর্বাভাস} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A forecast\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{জ্যোতিষী} (jyotishī)}{জ্যোতিষী (jyotishī)}]{\bn{জ্যোতিষী} (jyotishī) — an astrologer}

\label{lesson:BN-C532-jyotishi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to sense trouble coming, then the Bengali for a forecast.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{জ্যোতিষী}}
\textbf{\bn{জ্যোতিষী}} — \emph{jyotishī} — \textquotedblleft{}an astrologer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{জ্যোতিষী} \bn{আমার} \bn{হাত} \bn{দেখলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Jyotishī āmār hāt dekhlen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The astrologer read my palm.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{জ্যোতিষী}} (\emph{jyotishī}) is built on Sanskrit \emph{jyotiṣa}, which Monier-Williams glosses as \textquotedblleft{}an astronomer\textquotedblright{}, with the ending \emph{-ī}, \textquotedblleft{}one who does it\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jyotishī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Jyotishī āmār hāt dekhlen.} — The astrologer read my palm.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to sense trouble coming, then the Bengali for a forecast, then say \emph{jyotishī} again
\end{itemize}
